chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The divorce of the pregnant woman is one revocable divorce; if he wishes, he may take her back before she gives birth. If she gives birth before he takes her back, then she is definitively divorced from him, and he is one of the suitors.

key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: She is definitively divorced from him
key_terms.رَاجَعَهَا: He took her back (revoked the divorce)
key_terms.وَاحِدَةٌ: One (referring to a single revocable divorce)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on revoking divorce for a pregnant woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the mechanics of *Talaq al-Hamil* (divorce of a pregnant woman), establishing that the waiting period (*Iddah*) extends until childbirth, during which the divorce remains revocable. It highlights the practical implication that if the husband does not reconcile before the birth, the bond is severed, requiring him to court her anew as a stranger, a ruling derived from the Prophet's explicit instruction to Imam al-Sadiq.
